headline: Southborough boards prepared for October Special Town Meeting, opened hearings on a Costco proposal, and narrowed Neary School building options.
synopsis: Town officials finalized positions for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, with the Select Board and Advisory Committee splitting over funding requests for municipal golf irrigation, trail bridges, and two-family zoning amendments. The Planning Board opened public review on an 88-page proposal for a 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position gas station on Coslin Drive, drawing community concerns over traffic and noise. The Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate an exterior addition option for Neary School and focused design work on interior renovations, an enclosed courtyard gym, and a $15 million baseline. Department heads began preparing dual FY28 budget scenarios ahead of a potential spring Proposition 2 1/2 tax override, modeling severe service reductions if an override fails. School committees across Northborough and Southborough approved a $22,750 salary adjustment for Superintendent Gregory Martineau and paused plans to deploy a cell phone tracking app at Algonquin Regional High School.

top_items.title: Costco warehouse and gas station hearings open
top_items.why: The Planning Board began review of a 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-position fueling station spanning Southborough and Westborough.
top_items.body: Project consultants presented site plans, dark-sky lighting, and grading for the 26-acre parcel at 21 Coslin Drive, while board members and residents raised concerns over regional traffic, truck routing, and loading dock noise. The hearing was continued to October 19.

top_items.title: Neary School options narrowed to courtyard gym and renovation
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 3-1 to eliminate an exterior gym addition and focused study on interior options and a $15 million scope.
top_items.body: Consultants reported preliminary project cost estimates ranging from $24.4 million to $49.2 million, including a $4.5 million roof replacement. Architects highlighted that high groundwater and poor soils make exterior expansion challenging, while teachers expressed support for enclosing the interior courtyard into a 400-seat gymnasium.

top_items.title: Boards split on Special Town Meeting warrant articles
top_items.why: The Select Board and Advisory Committee took opposing stances on Community Preservation Act spending and zoning amendments ahead of Town Meeting.
top_items.body: The Advisory Committee voted against CPA funding requests of $433,346 for golf irrigation and $217,318 for the Peninsula Trail bridge, while the Select Board supported golf irrigation but opposed the trail bridge. The Advisory Committee also rejected a two-family zoning bylaw amendment that the Select Board supported 4-1.

top_items.title: CPA funding endorsed for golf irrigation and trail bridge
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee approved warrant articles to allocate CPA funds for golf course irrigation and a pedestrian footbridge.
top_items.body: The committee voted 4-1 to support $433,546 in additional CPA money alongside $100,000 from golf revolving funds for a $1.09 million irrigation overhaul, keeping Audubon certification conditions intact. The committee also voted 5-0 to back $217,318 for a 65-foot prefabricated bridge closing a gap on the Peninsula Trail.

top_items.title: Departments prepare dual FY28 budgets under override threat
top_items.why: Town departments began modeling two budget tracks for FY28 in anticipation of a potential spring Proposition 2 1/2 tax override vote.
top_items.body: Finance officials instructed departments to submit a level-services Budget A and a zero-increase Budget B. The Library Board of Trustees and Board of Health reviewed scenarios showing that without an override, departments would have to eliminate programming, staff training, and reduce employee operating hours to absorb rising costs.

top_items.title: School committees grant $22,750 salary adjustment to superintendent
top_items.why: Four regional school committees approved a retroactive market adjustment to Superintendent Gregory Martineau's employment contract.
top_items.body: Following executive session, the Northborough, Southborough, Regional, and Superintendency Union No. 3 committees approved the adjustment, bringing Martineau's 2026-2027 base salary to $270,213. Officials confirmed the adjustment will be funded from existing operational budgets without requiring additional local taxes.

top_items.title: Amy Berry appointed interim town clerk through May 2027
top_items.why: The Select Board unanimously appointed Amy Berry as interim town clerk following the retirement of long-time clerk Jim Hegarty.
top_items.body: Berry, who previously served as Southborough deputy town clerk and Grafton town clerk, will serve through May 11, 2027. The appointment comes as town boards finalized Town Meeting warrant articles proposing to change the town clerk role from an elected office to an appointed position.
